metadata.name: STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people

primary_reference.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. European Geriatric Medicine. 2023;14(4):625-632.

metadata.applicable_population: Adults aged 65 years and older. STOPP criteria identify potentially inappropriate medications (PIMs); START criteria identify potential prescribing omissions (PPOs). Apply only when patient is not end-of-life and the prescriber has confirmed all standard contraindications.

fields.id: Stable identifier of the form STOPP-<section><n> or START-<section><n>
fields.type: STOPP (potentially inappropriate medication) or START (potential prescribing omission)
fields.section_code: Letter code (A–M for STOPP, A–L for START) representing the physiological system or theme
fields.number_in_section: Sequential number within the section as published in v3
fields.statement: Clinical rule, with the trailing parenthetical rationale removed
fields.rationale: Clinical reasoning / evidence note as published in v3 (originally given in parentheses)
fields.tags: Derived semantic tags (drug class, condition, syndrome) to support indexing and CDS rule mapping

usage_notes: Each criterion is intended to trigger a structured medication review item; rationale is shown to clinicians as supporting evidence.
Criterion IDs are stable and safe to use as primary keys in a CDS rule table.
Section codes match the published v3 ordering and are NOT identical between STOPP and START (e.g. STOPP-K = falls drugs; START-K = analgesics).
Tags are heuristic and provided to bootstrap CDS rule mapping; review and extend before clinical deployment.

STOPP.name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people

criteria.statement: Any drug prescribed without a clinical indication
Any drug prescribed beyond the recommended duration, where treatment duration is well defined

Any duplicate drug class prescription for daily regular use (as distinct from PRN use) e.g., two concurrent NSAIDs, SSRIs, loop diuretics, ACE inhibitors, anticoagulants, antipsychotics, opioid analgesics
criteria.rationale: optimisation of monotherapy within a single drug class should be observed prior to considering a new agent

criteria.statement: Digoxin for heart failure with normal systolic ventricular function
Verapamil or diltiazem with NYHA Class III or IV heart failure
criteria.rationale: may worsen heart failure with reduced ejection fraction i.e., HFREF

criteria.statement: Beta-blocker in combination with verapamil or diltiazem
Ventricular rate-limiting drugs i.e., beta blocker, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin with bradycardia (< 50/min), type II heart block or complete heart block
criteria.rationale: risk of complete heart block, asystole

criteria.statement: Beta-blocker as monotherapy for uncomplicated hypertension i.e., not associated with angina pectoris, aortic aneurysm or other condition where beta-blocker therapy is indicated
Amiodarone as first-line antiarrhythmic therapy in supraventricular tachyarrhythmias
criteria.rationale: higher risk of major side-effects than beta-blockers, digoxin, verapamil or diltiazem

criteria.statement: Loop diuretic as first-line treatment for hypertension unless there is concurrent heart failure requiring diuretic therapy
Loop diuretic for dependent ankle oedema without clinical, biochemical or radiological evidence of heart failure, liver failure, nephrotic syndrome or renal failure
criteria.rationale: leg elevation and/or compression hosiery usually more appropriate

criteria.statement: Thiazide diuretic with current significant hypokalaemia (i.e., serum K+ < 3.0 mmol/l), hyponatraemia (i.e., serum Na+ < 130 mmol/l), hypercalcaemia (i.e., corrected serum calcium > 2.65 mmol/l) or with a history of gout
criteria.rationale: hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypercalcaemia and gout can be precipitated by thiazide diuretic

criteria.statement: Loop diuretic for treatment of hypertension with concurrent urinary incontinence
Centrally-acting antihypertensives e.g., methyldopa, clonidine, moxonidine, rilmenidine, guanfacine
criteria.rationale: centrally-active antihypertensives are generally less well tolerated by older people than younger people

criteria.statement: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs) or Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs) in patients with hyperkalaemia i.e., serum K > 5.5 mmol/l
Aldosterone antagonists (e.g., spironolactone, eplerenone) with concurrent potassium-conserving drugs (e.g., ACEI's, ARB's, amiloride, triamterene) without monitoring of serum potassium
criteria.rationale: risk of dangerous hyperkalaemia i.e., > 6.0 mmol/l – serum K should be monitored regularly, i.e., at least every 6 months

criteria.statement: Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors (e.g., sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) in severe heart failure characterised by hypotension i.e., systolic BP < 90 mmHg, or concurrent nitrate therapy for angina

Drugs that predictably prolong the QTc interval (QTc = QT/RR) in patients with known demonstrable QTc prolongation (to >450 msec in males and >470 msec in females), including quinolones, macrolides, ondansetron, citalopram (doses > 20 mg/day), escitalopram (doses > 10 mg/day), tricyclic antidepressants, lithium, haloperidol, digoxin, class 1A antiarrhythmics, class III antiarrhythmics, tizanidine, phenothiazines, astemizole, mirabegron
Statins for primary cardiovascular prevention in persons aged ≥ 85 and established frailty with expected life expectancy likely less than 3 years
Long-term systemic i.e., non-topical NSAIDs with known history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease
Long-term antipsychotics with known history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease
NSAIDs or systemic corticosteroids with heart failure requiring loop diuretic therapy
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbation of heart failure

criteria.statement: Antihypertensive drugs in severe symptomatic aortic stenosis
Digoxin as first line treatment for long-term (> 3 months) ventricular rate control in atrial fibrillation
criteria.rationale: increased mortality from long-term digoxin use; cardio-selective beta-blockers are generally preferable

criteria.statement: Long-term aspirin at doses greater than 100mg per day
criteria.rationale: increased risk of bleeding, no evidence for increased efficacy

criteria.statement: Antiplatelet agents, vitamin K antagonists, direct thrombin inhibitors or factor Xa inhibitors with concurrent significant risk of major bleeding, i.e. uncontrolled severe hypertension, bleeding diathesis, recent non-trivial spontaneous bleeding

Aspirin plus clopidogrel as long-term secondary stroke prevention i.e., > 4 weeks, unless the patient has a coronary stent(s) inserted in the previous 12 months or concurrent acute coronary syndrome or has a high grade symptomatic carotid arterial stenosis
criteria.rationale: no evidence of added long-term benefit over clopidogrel monotherapy

criteria.statement: Antiplatelet agents in combination with vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in patients with chronic atrial fibrillation, unless there is concurrent coronary artery stent(s) inserted or angiographically proven high grade (> 50%) coronary artery stenosis
criteria.rationale: no added benefit from antiplatelet agents

criteria.statement: Antiplatelet agents with vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in patients with stable coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral arterial disease
criteria.rationale: no evidence of added benefit from dual therapy

criteria.statement: Ticlopidine in any circumstances
criteria.rationale: clopidogrel and prasugrel have similar efficacy, stronger evidence and fewer side-effects

criteria.statement: Antiplatelet agents as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists, direct thrombin inhibitors or factor Xa inhibitors for stroke prevention in patients with chronic atrial fibrillation
Vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors for first deep venous thrombosis without continuing provoking risk factors (e.g., thrombophilia) for longer than 6 months
Vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors for first pulmonary embolus without continuing provoking risk factors (e.g., thrombophilia) for longer than 12 months
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in combination
Vitamin K antagonist as first-line anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation, unless there is concurrent metallic heart valve in-situ, moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, or eGFR < 15 mls/min./1.73m2
criteria.rationale: direct thrombin inhibitors or factor Xa inhibitors are equally efficacious and safer than vitamin K antagonists

criteria.statement: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in combination with Vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitor with a previous history of major haemorrhage
criteria.rationale: increased risk of bleeding due to antiplatelet effects of SSRIs

criteria.statement: Direct thrombin inhibitor (e.g., dabigatran) and diltiazem or verapamil

Apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) drug efflux pump inhibitors e.g., amiodarone, azithromycin, carvedilol, cyclosporin, dronedarone, itraconazole, ketoconazole (systemic), macrolides, quinine, ranolazine, tamoxifen, ticagrelor, verapamil
Systemic oestrogens or androgens with previous history of venous thromboembolism
criteria.rationale: increased risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism

criteria.statement: Aspirin for primary prevention in cardiovascular disease

TriCyclic Antidepressants (TCAs) in patients with dementia, narrow angle glaucoma, cardiac conduction abnormalities, prostatism, chronic constipation, recent falls, prior history of urinary retention or orthostatic hypotension
Initiation of TriCyclic Antidepressants (TCAs) as first-line treatment for major depression
criteria.rationale: higher risk of adverse drug reactions with TCAs than with SSRIs or SNRIs

criteria.statement: Serotonin/noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs e.g., venlafaxine, duloxetine) and severe hypertension i.e., systolic blood pressure > 180 mmHg +/- diastolic blood pressure > 105 mmHg

Antipsychotics with moderate-marked antimuscarinic/anticholinergic effects (acepromazine, chlorpromazine, clozapine, flupenthixol, fluphenzine, levomepromazine, olanzapine, pipothiazine, promazine, thioridazine) with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia or previous urinary retention
Antipsychotics prescribed for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) at an unchanged dose for > 3 months without medication review
criteria.rationale: increased risk of extrapyramidal side-effects and chronic worsening of cognition, increased risk of major cardiovascular morbidity and mortality

criteria.statement: Selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors (SSRIs) with current or recent significant hyponatraemia i.e., serum Na+ < 130 mmol/l
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbating or precipitating hyponatraemia

criteria.statement: Selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors (SSRIs) with current or recent significant bleeding
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbation or recurrence of bleeding due to antiplatelet effects of SSRIs

criteria.statement: Benzodiazepines for ≥ 4 weeks
criteria.rationale: no indication for longer treatment; risk of prolonged sedation, confusion, impaired balance, falls, road traffic accidents; all benzodiazepines should be withdrawn gradually if taken for more than 4 weeks as there is a risk of causing a benzodiazepine withdrawal syndrome if stopped abruptly

criteria.statement: Benzodiazepines for agitated behaviour or psychotic symptoms of dementia
Benzodiazepines for insomnia for ≥ 2 weeks
criteria.rationale: high risk of dependency, increased risk of falls, fractures and road traffic accidents

criteria.statement: Z-drugs (zolpidem, zopiclone, zaleplon) for insomnia for ≥ 2 weeks
Antipsychotics (i.e., other than clozapine or quetiapine) in those with parkinsonism or Dementia with Lewy Bodies
Anticholinergic/antimuscarinic drugs (biperiden, orphenadrine, procyclidine, trihexyphenidyl) to treat extra-pyramidal side-effects of antipsychotic medications

Drugs with potent anticholinergic/antimuscarinic effects (e.g., tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, doxepin, imipramine, nortriptyline; antipsychotics such as chlorpromazine, clozapine, thioridazine; first generation antihistamines such as diphenhydramine, chlorpheniramine; bladder antispasmodics such as tolterodine, oxybutynin; hyoscine, procyclidine, benzatropine, tizanidine) in patients with delirium or dementia
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbation of cognitive impairment

criteria.statement: Antipsychotics in patients with behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) for longer than 12 weeks unless BPSD symptoms are severe and other non-pharmacological treatments have failed
criteria.rationale: increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction

criteria.statement: Antipsychotics as hypnotics, unless sleep disorder is due to psychosis or BPSD effects of dementia
criteria.rationale: not recommended in summary of product characteristics; increased risk of confusion, hypotension, extra-pyramidal side effects, falls

criteria.statement: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors with a known history of persistent bradycardia (< 60 beats/min.), heart block or recurrent unexplained syncope
criteria.rationale: risk of cardiac conduction failure, syncope and injury

criteria.statement: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors with concurrent treatment with drugs that induce persistent bradycardia (< 60 beats/min.) such as beta-blockers, digoxin, diltiazem, verapamil
criteria.rationale: risk of cardiac conduction failure, syncope and injury

criteria.statement: Memantine with known current or previous seizure disorder
Nootropics in dementia including Gingko Biloba, piracetam, pramiracetam, phenylpiracetam, aniracetam, phosphatidylserine, modafinil, L-theanine, omega-3 fatty acids, panax ginseng, rhodiola, creatine
Phenothiazines as first-line treatment for psychosis or non-cognitive symptoms of dementia, since safer and more efficacious alternatives exist
criteria.rationale: phenothiazines are sedative, have significant anti-muscarinic toxicity in older people, except for prochlorperazine for nausea/vomiting/vertigo, chlorpromazine for relief of persistent hiccoughs and levomepromazine as an anti-emetic in palliative care

criteria.statement: Levodopa or dopamine agonists for benign essential tremor
Levodopa or dopamine agonists for treatment of extrapyramidal side-effects of antipsychotics or other forms of drug-induced Parkinsonism
criteria.rationale: inappropriate prescribing cascade to be avoided

criteria.statement: First-generation antihistamines as first-line treatment for allergy or pruritus
criteria.rationale: safer antihistamines with fewer side-effects now widely available

criteria.statement: First-generation antihistamines for insomnia
criteria.rationale: high risk of side-effects, Z-drugs safer and more appropriate for short-term use

criteria.statement: Digoxin at a long-term (i.e. more than 90 days) maintenance dose ≥ 125µg/day if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
criteria.rationale: risk of digoxin toxicity if plasma levels not measured

criteria.statement: Direct thrombin inhibitors (e.g., dabigatran) if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
Factor Xa inhibitors (e.g., rivaroxaban, apixaban, edoxaban) if eGFR < 15 ml/min/1.73m2
NSAIDs if eGFR < 50 ml/min/1.73m2
criteria.rationale: risk of deterioration in renal function

criteria.statement: Colchicine if eGFR < 10 ml/min/1.73m2
Metformin if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (e.g. spironolactone, eplerenone) if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
Nitrofurantoin if eGFR < 45 ml/min/1.73m2
Bisphosphonates if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
criteria.rationale: increased risk of acute renal failure

criteria.statement: Methotrexate if eGFR < 30 ml/min/1.73m2
Prochlorperazine or metoclopramide with Parkinsonism
Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) for uncomplicated peptic ulcer disease at full therapeutic dosage for > 8 weeks
criteria.rationale: dose reduction or earlier discontinuation or H2 antagonist maintenance therapy usually indicated

criteria.statement: Drugs likely to cause constipation (e.g. systemic antimuscarinics, oral iron, opioids, verapamil, aluminium antacids) with chronic constipation where non-constipating alternatives are available
Oral elemental iron doses greater than 200 mg daily
criteria.rationale: e.g. ferrous fumarate > 600 mg/day, ferrous sulphate > 600 mg/day, ferrous gluconate > 1800 mg/day; no evidence of enhanced iron absorption above these doses

criteria.statement: Corticosteroids with a history of peptic ulcer disease or erosive oesophagitis
criteria.rationale: risk of relapse unless proton pump inhibitor is co-prescribed

criteria.statement: Antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs with a history of Gastric Antral Vascular Ectasia (GAVE, "watermelon stomach")
Antipsychotics with dysphagia
Megestrol acetate to increase appetite
criteria.rationale: increased risk of thrombosis and death with unproven efficacy

criteria.statement: Theophylline as monotherapy for COPD
criteria.rationale: safer, more effective alternative; risk of adverse effects due to narrow therapeutic index

criteria.statement: Systemic corticosteroids instead of inhaled corticosteroids for maintenance therapy in moderate-severe COPD
criteria.rationale: unnecessary exposure to long-term side-effects of systemic corticosteroids and effective inhaled therapies are available

criteria.statement: Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (e.g., tiotropium, aclidinium, umeclidinium, glycopyrronium) with a history of narrow angle glaucoma (may exacerbate glaucoma) or bladder outflow obstruction
Benzodiazepines with acute or chronic respiratory failure i.e. pO2 < 8.0 kPa ± pCO2 > 6.5 kPa
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbation of respiratory failure

criteria.statement: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) other than COX-2 selective agents with history of peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding, unless with concurrent PPI or H2 antagonist
NSAIDs with severe hypertension i.e., systolic blood pressure consistently above 170 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure consistently above 100 mmHg
Long-term use of NSAID (>3 months) for symptom relief of osteoarthritis pain where paracetamol has not been tried
criteria.rationale: simple analgesics preferable and usually as effective for pain relief and safer

criteria.statement: Long-term corticosteroids (>3 months) as monotherapy for rheumatoid arthritis
Corticosteroids (other than periodic intra-articular injections for mono-articular pain) for osteoarthritis
Long-term NSAID or colchicine (>3 months) for chronic treatment of gout where there is no contraindication to a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor (e.g., allopurinol, febuxostat)
criteria.rationale: xanthine-oxidase inhibitors are first choice prophylactic drugs in gout

criteria.statement: NSAID with concurrent corticosteroids for treatment of arthritis/rheumatism of any kind
criteria.rationale: increased risk of peptic ulcer disease

criteria.statement: Oral bisphosphonates in patients with a current or recent history of upper gastrointestinal disease i.e. dysphagia, oesophagitis, gastritis, duodenitis, or peptic ulcer disease, or upper gastrointestinal bleeding
criteria.rationale: risk of relapse/exacerbation of oesophagitis, oesophageal ulcer, oesophageal stricture

criteria.statement: Long-term opioids for osteoarthritis
criteria.rationale: lack of evidence of efficacy, increased risk of serious side-effects

criteria.statement: Systemic antimuscarinic drugs (e.g., oxybutynin, tolterodine, trospium) with dementia or chronic cognitive impairment
Systemic antimuscarinic drugs (e.g., oxybutynin, tolterodine, trospium) with narrow-angle glaucoma
criteria.rationale: risk of acute exacerbation of glaucoma

criteria.statement: Systemic antimuscarinic drugs (e.g., oxybutynin, tolterodine, trospium) for lower urinary tract symptoms with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and high post-void residual volume i.e. > 200 ml
criteria.rationale: uncertain efficacy and increased risk of urinary retention in older men

criteria.statement: Systemic antimuscarinic drugs (e.g., oxybutynin, tolterodine, trospium) with constipation
Alpha-1 receptor antagonists other than silodosin (e.g., alfuzosin, doxazosin, indoramin, tamsulosin, terazosin) with symptomatic orthostatic hypotension or history of syncope
Mirabegron in labile or severe hypertension
Duloxetine with urinary urgency or urge incontinence
criteria.rationale: duloxetine is indicated in stress incontinence but not in urinary urgency or urge incontinence

criteria.statement: Antibiotic use in asymptomatic bacteriuria
Sulphonylureas with a long half-life (e.g., glibenclamide, chlorpropamide, glimepiride) with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Thiazolidenediones (e.g., rosiglitazone, pioglitazone) with heart failure
criteria.rationale: risk of exacerbation of heart failure

criteria.statement: Non-selective beta-blockers in diabetes mellitus with frequent hypoglycaemic episodes
Sodium glucose co-transporter (SGLT2) inhibitors (e.g., canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin) with symptomatic hypotension
Systemic oestrogens with a history of breast cancer
Systemic oestrogens with a history of venous thromboembolism
Menopausal hormone therapy (oestrogen plus progestin) with a history of stenotic coronary, cerebral or peripheral arterial disease
criteria.rationale: increased risk of acute arterial thrombosis

criteria.statement: Systemic oestrogens without progestogens in patients with intact uterus
Levothyroxine in subclinical hypothyroidism i.e., normal free T4, elevated TSH but < 10 mU/L
criteria.rationale: no evidence of benefit, risk of iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis

criteria.statement: Vasopressin analogues (e.g., desmopressin, vasopressin) for urinary incontinence or urinary frequency

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Benzodiazepines in patients with recurrent falls
criteria.rationale: may cause reduced sensorium, impair balance

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Antipsychotic drugs in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Vasodilator drugs in patients with recurrent falls with persistent postural hypotension i.e., systolic BP drop ≥ 20 mmHg and/or diastolic BP drop ≥ 10 mmHg

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Hypnotic Z-drugs i.e., zopiclone, zolpidem, zaleplon in patients with recurrent falls
criteria.rationale: may cause protracted daytime sedation, ataxia

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Anti-epileptic drugs in patients with recurrent falls
criteria.rationale: may impair sensorium, may adversely affect cerebellar function

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: First generation antihistamines in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Opioids in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Antidepressants in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Alpha blockers as antihypertensives in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Alpha blockers for prostatic bladder outflow symptoms, other than silodosin in patients with recurrent falls

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Centrally acting antihypertensives in patients with recurrent falls
criteria.rationale: may impair sensorium and may cause orthostatic hypotension

criteria.section_name: Drugs that predictably increase falls risk in susceptible older people
criteria.statement: Antimuscarinics for treatment of overactive bladder or urge incontinence in patients with recurrent falls
Use of oral or transdermal strong opioids (morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl, buprenorphine, diamorphine, methadone, tramadol, pethidine, pentazocine) as first line therapy for mild pain
criteria.rationale: WHO analgesic ladder not observed; paracetamol or NSAID not prescribed as first-line therapy

criteria.statement: Use of daily regular (as distinct from PRN) opioids without concomitant laxative
Long-acting opioids without short-acting opioids for break-through moderate or severe pain
criteria.rationale: risk of persistence of severe pain

criteria.statement: Topical lidocaine (lignocaine) patch for treatment of chronic osteoarthritis pain
Gabapentinoids (e.g., gabapentin, pregabalin) for non-neuropathic pain
Paracetamol at doses ≥ 3 g/24 hours in patients with poor nutritional status i.e., BMI < 18 or chronic liver disease

Concomitant use of two or more drugs with antimuscarinic/anticholinergic properties (e.g., bladder antispasmodics, intestinal antispasmodics, tricyclic antidepressants, first generation antihistamines, antipsychotics)

Where a drug is clearly indicated and considered appropriate in the particular clinical context and there is no clear contraindication, that drug should be initiated as per formulary guidelines for dose and duration

Antihypertensive therapy where systolic blood pressure > 140 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure > 90 mmHg, unless established moderate or severe physical frailty in whom the threshold for therapy is 150 mmHg systolic pressure and/or 90 mmHg diastolic pressure
Statin therapy with a documented history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease, unless the patient's status is end-of-life or established moderate or severe frailty
Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitor with coronary artery disease
Beta-blocker with symptomatic coronary artery disease
Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitor for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Cardio-selective beta-blocker (bisoprolol, nebivolol, metoprolol or carvedilol) for stable heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone, eplerenone) in heart failure without severe renal function impairment i.e., eGFR > 30 ml/min/m2
SGLT-2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin) in symptomatic heart failure with or without reduced ejection fraction regardless of diabetes being present or not
Sacubitril/valsartan in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction causing persistent heart failure symptoms despite optimal dose of ACE inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker
criteria.rationale: Sacubitril/valsartan to replace ACE inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker

criteria.statement: Beta-blocker for chronic atrial fibrillation with uncontrolled heart rate
Intravenous iron for symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and iron deficiency
Vitamin K antagonists or direct thrombin inhibitors or factor Xa inhibitors in the presence of chronic or paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin or clopidogrel or prasugrel or ticagrelor) with a documented history of coronary, cerebral or peripheral vascular disease
L-DOPA or a dopamine agonist in idiopathic Parkinson's disease with functional impairment and resultant disability
Non-TCA antidepressant for major depression
Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine) for mild-moderate Alzheimer's dementia
Rivastigmine for Dementia with Lewy Bodies or Parkinson's disease dementia
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (or SNRI or pregabalin if SSRI contraindicated) for persistent severe anxiety that affects independent functioning and quality of life
Dopamine agonist (ropinirole or pramipexole or rotigotine) for Restless Legs Syndrome, once iron deficiency and severe chronic kidney disease (i.e., eGFR < 30 ml/min/m2) have been excluded
Propranolol for essential tremor with functional impairment and resultant disability

One-alpha hydroxycholecalciferol or calcitriol supplementation in severe chronic kidney disease (i.e., eGFR < 30 ml/min/m2) with hypocalcaemia (corrected serum calcium < 2.10 mmol/l) and associated secondary hyperparathyroidism
Phosphate binder in severe chronic kidney disease (i.e., eGFR < 30 ml/min/m2) if serum phosphate concentration persistently > 1.76 mmol/l (5.5 mg/dl) despite adherence to renal diet

Erythropoietin analogue in severe chronic kidney disease (i.e., eGFR < 30 ml/min/m2) with symptomatic anaemia not attributable to haematinic or iron deficiency to achieve a haemoglobin concentration of 10.0 to 12.0 g/dl
Angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) or Angiotensin Converting Enzyme Inhibitor (ACE-I) in chronic kidney disease with proteinuria i.e., urine albumin excretion > 300 mg/24 hours
Proton Pump Inhibitor with severe gastro-oesophageal reflux disease or peptic oesophageal stricture requiring dilatation
Proton pump inhibitor with initiation of low-dose aspirin and previous history of peptic ulcer or reflux oesophagitis
Proton pump inhibitor with short-term (< 2 weeks) or longer-term (> 2 weeks) NSAID
Fibre supplements (e.g., bran, ispaghula, methylcellulose, sterculia) for diverticulosis with a history of constipation
Osmotic laxative (e.g., lactulose, macrogol, sorbitol) for chronic persistent idiopathic or secondary benign constipation
Probiotics used with antibiotics in patients who are not immunocompromised or severely debilitated for the prevention of Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhoea
Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy in HP-associated active peptic ulcer disease

Long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA e.g., tiotropium, aclidinium, umeclidinium, glycopyrronium) or long-acting beta 2 agonist (LABA e.g., bambuterol, formoterol, indacaterol, olodaterol, salmeterol) for symptomatic COPD of GOLD 1 or 2 severity and chronic asthma

Regular i.e. daily inhaled corticosteroid (e.g., beclomethasone, budesonide, ciclesonide, fluticasone, mometasone) for moderate-severe asthma or COPD of GOLD 3 or 4 severity, where FEV1 < 50% of predicted value and repeated exacerbations requiring treatment with oral corticosteroids
Home continuous oxygen with documented chronic hypoxaemia
criteria.rationale: i.e., pO2 < 8.0 kPa or 60 mmHg or SaO2 < 89%

criteria.statement: Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) with chronic, active and disabling rheumatoid arthritis
Bisphosphonates and vitamin D and calcium in patients taking long-term systemic corticosteroid therapy for prevention of steroid-induced osteoporosis
Vitamin D in patients with known osteoporosis and/or previous fragility fracture(s) and/or Bone Mineral Density T-scores below -2.5 in one or multiple sites

Bone anti-resorptive or anabolic therapy (e.g., bisphosphonate, teriparatide, denosumab) in patients with documented osteoporosis (Bone Mineral Density T-scores below -2.5 in one or multiple sites) and/or previous history of fragility fracture(s) – where no pharmacological or clinical status contraindication exists such as poor one-year life expectancy
Vitamin D supplement in older people with confirmed 25-hydroxycolecalciferol deficiency (< 20 micrograms/L, < 50 nmol/L) who are housebound or experiencing falls or with osteopenia
criteria.rationale: Bone Mineral Density T-score is less than -1.0 but above -2.5 in one or multiple sites

criteria.statement: Anti-resorptive treatment after discontinuation of at least two doses of denosumab
criteria.rationale: rebound increased bone turnover markers, BMD loss, and increased risk of vertebral fracture following denosumab discontinuation

criteria.statement: Anti-resorptive treatment after discontinuation of teriparatide/abaloparatide treatment for osteoporosis
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors (e.g. allopurinol, febuxostat) with a history of recurrent episodes of gout
Folic acid supplement in patients taking methotrexate

Selective alpha-1 receptor blocker (e.g., tamsulosin, silodosin) for lower urinary tract symptoms related to benign prostatic hyperplasia where prostatectomy is not considered necessary or appropriate or safe

5-alpha reductase inhibitor (e.g., finasteride, dutasteride) for lower urinary tract symptoms related to benign prostatic hyperplasia where prostatectomy is not considered necessary or appropriate or safe
Topical vaginal oestrogen or vaginal oestrogen pessary for symptomatic atrophic vaginitis
Topical vaginal oestrogen or vaginal oestrogen pessary in women for recurrent urinary tract infections
Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors (e.g., avanafil, sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) for persistent erectile dysfunction that causes distress

ACE inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (if intolerant of ACE inhibitor) in diabetes with evidence of renal disease i.e., dipstick proteinuria or microalbuminuria (> 30 mg/24 hours) unless evidence of severe CKD
High-potency opioids in moderate-severe non-arthritis pain, where paracetamol, NSAIDs or low-potency opioids are not appropriate to the pain severity or have been ineffective
Laxatives in patients receiving opioids regularly i.e., other than PRN use
Topical 5% lidocaine (lignocaine) patch for localized neuropathic pain, e.g. post-herpetic neuralgia
Seasonal influenza vaccine annually
Pneumococcal vaccine at least once according to national guidelines
Varicella-zoster vaccine according to national guidelines
SARS-CoV2 vaccine according to national guidelines
